newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar mixed in Tokyo, upward trend intact vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar mixed in Tokyo, upward trend intact vs yen.

text.p: *Dollar edged up versus yen in mid-morning Tokyo on Wednesday due to short-covering led by traders and interbank operators.
*Dollar carried over its overnight firmness against yen.
*But dollar capped as exporters continued selling sporadically on rallies.
*Greenback edged down against mark due to mark's firmness against yen. Strong technical resistance for mark/yen seen at around 64.80.
*"Short-holders seem to have squared their positions after the dollar climbed sharply against the yen overnight," a Japanese commercial bank dealer said.
*Dollar drifts lower on profit-taking sales in early morning Tokyo, trimming overnight gains, dealers said.

*Offers from exporters and Japanese investors expected on upside, weighing on dollar/yen. But a dealer at a long-term credit bank said actual offers from investors for hedge purposes not yet detected.

*Dollar/mark's topside heavy ahead of Germany's planned statement later in day calling for strong mark and strong euro. *But dollar's undertone still firm, with buying interest on dips intact, dealers said.

*Dealers said although they are focusing on Japanese and U.S. trade data due out later this week, impact from U.S.-Japan trade issues may be limited after series of recent comments from MOF senior official Eisuke Sakakibara.
*Sakakibara, newly appointed vice finance minister for international affairs, has repeatedly said ministry has no intention to use foreign exchange rates as trade tool.
*Japan's customs-cleared trade balance for June is due out on Thursday, while U.S. international trade data for May will be released on Friday.
